# Laurel 套件 · 给 DeepSeek Harness 的「功能管理」面板 + 五个功能插件 说人话:装上它,Harness 的设置里会多出一个**功能管理**面板,面板里五行开关, 分别控制五个小功能。每个功能都能单独开、单独关,也能单独更新 —— 不喜欢一个,关掉就行,不影响别的。 | 开关 | 它干什么 | |---|---| | **通知** | 你在忙别的窗口时,AI 有问题要问你、等你批准、或者干完了,弹一条 Windows 通知并响一声,不用一直盯着 | | **Claude 主题** | 把界面换成暖黄的纸面配色 + 更适合阅读的正文排版。只改外观,不碰你的数据和别的插件 | | **记忆与上下文** | 让 AI 跨会话记得事:本会话 → 本工作区 → 全局,三级范围;读别的项目需要你逐次授权。数据只存在你自己电脑上 | | **内耗护栏** | 治「干等、串扰、返工」:给子代理的等待套上限、把结论赶去写文件、按文件计返工次数、上下文每长一段就提醒一次、共享目录加锁。三档预设(温和/均衡/严格)+ 逐项自定义 | | **可视化规划模式** | 把一个大任务画成节点图,拆成能并行的小批次;方案要你**采纳并批准**才开工,做完有审计报告。体积大,默认关着 | 五个功能出厂**全是关的**——你想用哪个,自己打开。 --- ## 装它(三步,照着做就行) > **先说一句前提**:这套东西是「一个面板 + 五个插件」。在 Harness 看来是**六个包**, > 所以要**一次把六个都装上**;只装面板那一个,面板里那六行会解析不到,点了没反应。 **第 1 步:拿到代码** ```bash git clone https://github.com/Sakayorilove/dsh-laurel ``` (不想用命令行:在仓库页面点绿色的 `Code` → `Download ZIP`,解压到一个长期不动的目录。) **第 2 步:把六个包装进你的 Harness**(Windows 侧,不是 WSL 里) 先确认两个前置能跑(`node -v` 要 ≥ 22.19;没装 pnpm 的话先 `npm i -g pnpm`): ```powershell node -v pnpm -v ``` 打开 PowerShell,进到刚下载的文件夹,跑: ```powershell node scripts/install-profile.mjs ``` 它会自己找到你的 Harness profile,写好六个依赖、跑一次安装、再校验一遍; **中途出错会整体回滚**,不会把你的环境弄坏。它只动这六个包,你其它的依赖一个都不碰。 几种情况: | 情况 | 怎么办 | |---|---| | 找不到 profile,或找到**多个**候选 | 它会列出候选并停下,**不会猜**。把正确的那个显式传进去:
`node scripts/install-profile.mjs "C:\Users\<用户名>\.dsh\profiles\desktop"` | | 只想校验,不想改任何东西 | `node scripts/install-profile.mjs --check` | | 安装目录不在仓库里 | 加 `--center <目录>`,例如 `--center D:\Laurel-Center` | | 机器上有**多份** pnpm(比如 Harness 客户端自带一份、全局又装了一份) | 版本不同可能把**整个 profile 的 lockfile 重写一遍**(profile 里往往还有别的插件)。指定用哪份,再照常跑:
`$env:LAUREL_PNPM = "C:\...\resources\runtime\pnpm\bin\pnpm.cjs"` | | 缺 pnpm | 安装器会先报出来(退出码 5)再退出,**不会**改到一半停住 | **第 3 步:完全退出 Harness,再打开** 注意是**完全退出**(右下角托盘也退掉),不是关窗口。然后进 **设置 → 功能管理**,把想要的功能打开。 开了之后:界面上能立刻看到的(主题、面板本身)**刷新一下页面**就生效; 需要重启才生效的(通知、记忆这类后台逻辑)会在提示里说明。 --- ## 装完发现不对? | 现象 | 多半是因为 | |---|---| | 面板里没有五行,或者点了开关没反应 | 只装了面板,没装五个模块 → 重跑第 2 步的安装命令 | | 点某个开关,提示「操作未成功：XX:operation-error」 | 那个模块的包**还没装进 profile**(源码里有它、profile 里没有)。先**完全退出** Harness,重跑第 2 步的安装命令,再启动。界面上的提示会把宿主的原始报错带在括号里,一般能直接看出是哪个包 | | 打开了但界面没变化 | 没有完全退出重开;或只刷新了页面但改的是后台半边 | | 五个功能显示「已关闭」 | 这是出厂默认,自己在面板里打开就行 | | 主题没生效 | 它有两道开关:功能管理里打开,「设置 → Claude 羊皮纸」里也要勾上 | | 想让 Harness 回到装之前的样子 | `node scripts/install-profile.mjs --rollback` 回滚;`--uninstall` 移除六个依赖(两个命令都不用再传 profile 路径) | **支持范围**:这套在 **DeepSeek Harness 桌面版 0.2.0-rc.2**(Windows + WSL2)上验证过。 更早或更新的版本没测过 —— 宿主升级后如果界面细节回退,通常是客户端类名变了,来提 Issue 就行。 --- ## 给 AI 助手看的精确指令 > 你要让 AI 帮你装,把下面整段原样发给它。这一节是**机器可读版本**,保留了全部路径与参数。 ```text 任务:在 Windows 上把 Laurel 套件装进 DeepSeek Harness。 前提(必须遵守): - 本套件在宿主看来是六个直接依赖:laurel-center(装载机/面板) + laurel + dsh-claude-parchment + dsh-strata + dsh-warden + dsh-loom(五个模块)。只装 laurel-center 会导致它插入的其余六行解析不到。 - 改的是 Windows 的 profile,所以 pnpm 必须在 Windows 侧跑; 不要在 WSL 里对 Windows profile 跑 pnpm(会写出 Windows 解析不了的链接)。 - 需要 Node ≥ 22.19 与可用的 pnpm(`pnpm -v` 能跑;没有就先 `npm i -g pnpm`)。 缺 pnpm 时安装器会先报错退出(退出码 5),不会改到一半停住。 步骤: 1. 克隆仓库并进入目录: git clone https://github.com/Sakayorilove/dsh-laurel cd <仓库目录> 2. 跑安装事务(它会写六个依赖 → pnpm install → 校验,失败整体回滚): node scripts/install-profile.mjs # 它会自己找 profile;找不到或找到多个候选时它会列出来并停下,把正确的那个显式传进去: # node scripts/install-profile.mjs "C:\Users\<用户名>\.dsh\profiles\desktop" # 安装目录不在仓库里时: --center <仓库绝对路径> # 只校验不改动: --check # 回滚: --rollback # 卸载: --uninstall 3. 校验装配(只读): node scripts/verify-installed.mjs 期望:六个依赖的 realpath 分别落在 <仓库> 与 <仓库>/packages/<模块>,patch 六行、模块默认 disabled。 4. 告诉用户:完全退出 Harness 再打开,然后进「设置 → 功能管理」打开需要的功能。 客户端半边刷新页面即生效;宿主半边(通知/记忆等)需要完全重启。 等价的手工做法(profile 的 package.json,六个都要有;放 dependencies 或 devDependencies 都行, 但**每个只能出现一处** —— 两段都有同一个名字时,后面那段会盖掉前面那段): "dependencies": { "laurel-center": "link:<仓库绝对路径>", "laurel": "link:<仓库绝对路径>/packages/laurel", "dsh-claude-parchment": "link:<仓库绝对路径>/packages/dsh-claude-parchment", "dsh-strata": "link:<仓库绝对路径>/packages/dsh-strata", "dsh-warden": "link:<仓库绝对路径>/packages/dsh-warden", "dsh-loom": "link:<仓库绝对路径>/packages/dsh-loom" } 并确保 "dsh.profile.bundles" 里有 "laurel-center",且没有把六个模块另写成 bundle 行。 只读自检(不需要装任何依赖,克隆下来就能跑): node scripts/check.mjs # 期望:通过 236 项,失败 0 项 node scripts/integration-probe.mjs # 期望:通过 32 项 node scripts/bootgraph-probe.mjs # 期望:通过 37 项 node scripts/module.mjs check # 期望:0 问题 安装事务的隔离复现(需要 pnpm;在临时目录里跑真实的安装/迁移/卸载/回滚,**不碰任何真实 profile**): node scripts/install-probe.mjs # 期望:全部场景通过(九个场景) 相关环境变量(可选): DSH_LOOM_WSL_USER 指定 WSL 用户(默认用该发行版的默认用户) DSH_LOOM_WSL_WORKTREE_BASE 指定 Loom 工作树的 WSL 侧基础目录 LAUREL_CENTER_INSTALL 指定安装面目录(默认从 profile 推导) 不要做的事: - 不要手改安装面里的文件(它由 node scripts/release.mjs 从源码生成) - 不要手改构建产物 lib/client.js(改源码后跑 node scripts/build-client.mjs) ``` --- ## 常见配置 - **通知提示音**：「设置 → 通知」里可以填一个 wav 文件的绝对路径； Windows 自带的在 `C:\Windows\Media\` 下,例如 `C:/Windows/Media/Windows Notify Calendar.wav`。 - **记忆数据**：存在 `$DSH_HOME/strata/memories.jsonl`,是**追加式**的——遗忘会追加一条事件,不删旧行,方便你以后核对。 - **Loom 的工作树**：默认放在插件自己的数据目录;想放到 WSL 里(更快)就设 `DSH_LOOM_WSL_WORKTREE_BASE`,例如 `/home/<你的 WSL 用户>/projects/.dsh-loom`。 --- ## 给开发者 ```bash node scripts/check.mjs # 装载机离线自检(248 项,含全仓 JS 语法) node scripts/integration-probe.mjs # patch 组出 loader 树、开关语义 node scripts/bootgraph-probe.mjs # boot graph 行、bundle id、inject 值域 node scripts/module.mjs check # 五个模块的落点是否一致 node scripts/install-probe.mjs # 安装事务的隔离复现(真实 pnpm,临时目录,需 pnpm) node scripts/build-client.mjs # 改了客户端源码后重建产物 node scripts/release.mjs --to <目录> # 从源码生成只含运行文件的安装面 ``` 上面几条里只有 `install-probe.mjs` 需要 pnpm(要真的建链接);其余克隆下来就能跑,不用装依赖。 CI 在 push 到 main 和每个 PR 上跑四个 job: | job | 跑什么 | |---|---| | 离线门禁 | 上面那四条 + 客户端产物与源码一致(不需要装依赖) | | 安装事务 | `install-probe.mjs`,真实 pnpm,隔离 profile | | 模块测试 | 五个包各自的测试:通知、记忆、主题(含真实 Chromium 用例)、护栏(离线,零依赖)、Loom(含 tsc) | | 宿主集成 | **手动触发**,需要一台装了 Harness 的自托管 runner,`--require-host` | 各模块自己的测试需要额外依赖,见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。 ⚠ 这四个 job 目前**还没有在 GitHub 上真正执行过**(仓库刚公开,CI 环境未验证); 本机已按同一组命令跑通,但别把它当成"已经绿了的徽章"。 | 文档 | 内容 | |---|---| | [MODULES.md](MODULES.md) | 装载机与模块的关系、单独更新、增删模块、标签约定 | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | 变化记录 | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | 环境、提交前必跑的检查、硬规矩 | | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) | 安全问题怎么报、各模块接触哪些数据 | | [THIRD-PARTY.md](THIRD-PARTY.md) | 第三方接口与参考(不打包任何第三方运行时依赖) | | [docs/PLUGIN-CONTRACT.md](docs/PLUGIN-CONTRACT.md) | 与 DSH 客户端模块系统的接线契约 | ## 许可 MIT,见 [LICENSE](LICENSE);每个模块的 `packages/<目录>/LICENSE` 同样保留。

plugins.description: 设置DSH Harness对话流字体、字号行间距，以及对话文字到窗口边缘的留白。
plugins.readme_text:
# 对话流排版 · dsh-chat-typography

给 DSH Harness 的对话流加一页排版设置：**一个字号管住全文、一条网格管住所有纵向间距、三种角色各自的字体，以及对话文字到窗口边缘的留白**；此外还固定收紧了几处宿主留白（标题栏、代码块内边距、表格单元格、行内代码药丸底色）。

装好后「设置」里会多出一页 **对话流排版**。

![设置界面](docs/settings.png)

> 上图是设置页的四组控件（来源：浅色主题、Windows、默认值 + 代码字体 `Consolas`）。截图只展示设置项本身，上面提到的几处**固定收紧**（标题栏、代码块内边距、表格单元格、行内代码）作用于对话流，不在这张图里。

## 功能

### 字号：一个值管全部

宿主本身有一套刻意的字号阶梯 —— 标题 21 / 19 / 18px、正文 14px、次要文字 13px、行内代码 12px、代码块 11px。本插件把它**全部压到同一个值**：

```css
[data-chat-flow][data-chat-flow] *:not(textarea):not(input):not(svg):not(svg *) {
  font-size: var(--dsh-content-font-size, 14px) !important;
}
```

改的只是字号，不动字重和字体族：标题照样加粗，代码照样等宽。范围 10–22px。输入控件与图标（`svg`）被排除在外，不参与统一。

这个值写进 Harness 的主题设置，所以**和「外观」页共用同一份** —— 在哪一边改，另一边都跟着显示。

### 字体：文字 / 代码 / 终端 三种角色

三个输入框分别设置 `text` / `code` / `terminal` 的字体族，留空即系统默认。写入走 Harness 的主题服务，所以**和「外观」页共用同一份设置** —— 在这一页改，外观页同步显示；在外观页改，这里也会跟着变。输入不需要自己加引号，服务会做清洗和补引号。

### 行距与间距：所有纵向间隔只走一条网格

这是本插件最花力气的部分。宿主的纵向间距来自三处互不相干的地方：

| 来源 | 宿主取值 |
| --- | --- |
| 行盒 | `line-height: calc(24px + 字号增量)` |
| markdown 块边距 | 段落 16px、列表项之间 6px、标题上 32px |
| 对话流项之间 | `--dsh-chat-flow-gap`：6px / 12px / 16px 三种语境 |

三者叠加的结果是：**同一个段落里换行是一个间隔，两段之间是第二个，两条消息之间是第三个。** 插件把这三处收敛成同一个数：

- 行盒 = `max((16px + 字号增量) × 倍率, 字号)` —— 跟着字号联动，同时保证不会小到装不下文字
- markdown 文本块（`p`、`ul/ol`、`blockquote`、`h1–h6`、列表项之间）的边距**归零**，于是段内换行和段间换行的步长完全相等
- `--dsh-chat-flow-gap` **归零**，于是两条消息之间、正文与工具行之间，也只隔一个行盒
- 例外：代码块 / 表格 / 分隔线保留 `16px × 倍率` 的上下边距 —— 它们自带边框或底色，归零会让框和正文粘在一起

倍率范围 0.80–2.00，步进 0.05，存在 localStorage 的 `dsh-chat-typography.lineHeight`。**1.00 也是这条统一网格**，不会退回宿主原本参差的间距。

### 固定收紧的几处留白

下面这些**与倍率无关**，是固定值，也没有开关：

| 位置 | 宿主 | 现在 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 对话标题栏上下留白（无标签行时） | 各 10px（栏高 51px） | 各 5px（栏高 41px） |
| 代码块内部上下内边距 | 16px | 8px |
| 表格单元格内边距 | `10px 16px` | `5px 8px` |
| 行内代码 | 底色 + 描边 + 5px 左右内边距 | 无底色、无描边、无内边距 |

**标题栏**那条带 `:not(:has(.wSkVaW_tabs))` 守卫：宿主只在存在标签行时（`tabs.length > 1`）才把标题栏下限锁在 76px。不加守卫的话，一旦某个会话展开出标签行，这个下限会被覆盖掉，标签行就会和内容撞在一起。加守卫后实测：无标签 41px，有标签仍为 76px 不变。

**表格**只收内边距，不动边框。宿主另外把首列左边距和末列右边距归零（让表格左右贴齐），本层的选择器比宿主那两条更深，所以收内边距时会顺带破坏贴齐——因此贴齐也由本层手工还原。

**行内代码**去底色是因为宿主对它的处理本来就不一致：普通行内代码画成带底色和描边的"药丸"，而被判为可解析文件路径的那些（deliverables 会把它们改写成带 `_fileMention_` 的按钮）底色与描边被重置掉了。两段看起来一模一样的代码穿着两种不同的衣服，所以干脆都去掉。

### 恢复默认

一键把三个字号回默认（14 / 11 / 13）、清空三个字体族、行距回 1.00、留白清空。

### 左右留白

数字框设置对话文字距窗口左右边缘的距离（px），留空即宿主的默认宽度。宿主原来的对话列宽是 `clamp(680px, 视口宽 × 0.64, 920px)`，窗口一宽，两侧就空出很大一块；这一项把它收窄。

实现是覆写 `--dsh-chat-content-width`：对话流列、输入框卡片、用户气泡堆、宽表格都从这一个变量取宽度，所以它们会一起收窄并保持互相对齐。宿主已经为输入框两侧控件预留了 `--dsh-composer-side-clearance + 16px`（约 32px），所以填 0 也不会小于这个下限。设置此项后，宿主的「拖宽」手柄不再生效。

## 设置项一览

| 设置项 | 控件 | 范围与默认 | 存放位置 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 字号 | 数字框 | 10–22px，默认 14（宿主默认） | Harness 主题设置（与「外观」共用） |
| 字体 · 文字 / 代码 / 终端 | 文本框 | 留空 = 系统默认 | 同上 |
| 行距 | 数字框 | 0.80–2.00，步进 0.05，默认 1.00 | localStorage `dsh-chat-typography.lineHeight` |
| 左右留白 | 数字框 | 0–600px，留空 = 宿主默认 | localStorage `dsh-chat-typography.gutter` |

数字框回车或失焦提交；输入非法值会退回原值。

## 安装

在 Harness 的插件管理器里安装，`target` 传包名：

```
@zheshiyigehenchang/dsh-chat-typography
```

也可以从源码安装：先把本仓库 clone 到本地，再往管理器里传**包目录的绝对路径**（例如 `<你的克隆目录>\dsh-chat-typography`），管理器会：

1. 往 `<DSH_HOME>\profiles\<profile>\package.json` 的 `dependencies` 写入 `"@zheshiyigehenchang/dsh-chat-typography": "link:<包目录>"`
2. 把包名追加进该文件的 `dsh.profile.bundles`
3. 执行 pnpm 链接，`node_modules\@zheshiyigehenchang\dsh-chat-typography` 变成指向源码目录的符号链接

包目录不必放在 workspace 里；链接之后**源码即产物**，改 `client.js` 刷新页面就生效，不需要重新安装。

装完**刷新页面**即可，不需要重启 Harness。验证：打开设置，导航里应出现「对话流排版」。

## 目录结构

```
dsh-chat-typography/
├── package.json          包清单：exports / files / dsh.bundle.patch / dsh.client
├── cordis.patch.yml      向 profile 插入 bundle 行的 patch
├── index.js              Host 半个 bundle（本插件没有 Host 逻辑，只有空 apply）
├── client.js             全部实现：设置页 + 若干层样式
├── locale/
│   ├── zh.json           插件列表里的显示名与简介
│   └── en.json
├── icon.svg              插件列表图标
└── docs/                 README 里的截图
```

`client.js` 里叠了若干层样式，各自独立注入一个 `<style data-plugin-css=...>`：

| 层 | 作用域 | 是否常驻 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 统一字号 | `[data-chat-flow]` 内除输入控件与图标 | 常驻 |
| 行距与间距 | `[data-chat-flow]`，内容随倍率重写 | 常驻（倍率 1.00 也写） |
| 行内代码去底色 | `[data-chat-flow]` 内 markdown 的 `:not(pre)>code` 与文件提及 | 常驻 |
| 表格单元格收紧 | `[data-chat-flow]` 内 markdown 表格 | 常驻 |
| 代码卡片内部收紧 | `[data-chat-flow]` 内代码块的 `<pre>` 上下内边距 | 常驻 |
| 标题栏收紧 | `header.wSkVaW_header`（无标签行时） | 常驻 |
| 左右留白 | `:has([data-chat-flow])` 上的 `--dsh-chat-content-width` | 仅在填了数值时 |

后面这几层（行内代码、表格、代码卡片、标题栏）是**固定的紧凑化**，不提供开关，也不随任何设置变化。其共同做法是靠提高选择器特异性取胜（重复属性选择器 `[data-chat-flow][data-chat-flow]`、重复类名 `header.wSkVaW_header.wSkVaW_header`），**不使用 `!important`** —— 因为被覆盖的宿主规则本身都不是 `!important`。

**一个需要注意的坑：正文段落节奏的归零并不在常驻层里，而是「行距与间距」层的一部分。** 因此它跟着倍率走（倍率 1.00 同样生效），但如果行距层整个不挂载，正文节奏会退回宿主的 16px。

> 维护提示：`TIGHT_CODE_CARD_CSS` 里那两条 margin 规则其实是**死代码**。行距层已经归零了同样的文本块，而且选择器更深、注入更晚，实测开不开这两条规则结果完全一致。它们还表达了**相反**的意图（把 `.md-code-block` 和 `hr` 也归零），一旦样式表顺序变化就会静默生效，让分隔线和代码卡片贴上正文。真正属于这一层的只有 `<pre>` 的上下内边距那一条。

## 兼容性与已知限制

- **强依赖宿主内部实现**：`[data-chat-flow]` 钩子，`--dsh-chat-flow-gap`、`--dsh-chat-content-width`、`--dsl-terminal-line-height` 变量，以及 `[class*="_markdown_"]` 这类 CSS Modules 类名半段。宿主大版本升级（尤其是 `dsh-client-ui-chat` 与 `dsh-client-ui-primitives`）可能让某一层失效。类名用的是 localName 半段而不是哈希，跨构建稳定；变量名一旦改了就要跟着改。
- **改动全在浏览器侧**，生效方式是刷新页面。
- 单行的控件行（时间戳、复制/重试按钮行、工具卡标题行）高度由按钮决定，不随行距伸缩。
- 展开状态的步骤进程标题自带 `padding-bottom: 8px`，是固定值，也不随倍率走。
- 字体族的写入依赖主题服务暴露 `setFontFamily`；万一没有，字体分组会自动隐藏，其余功能不受影响。
- 标题栏那一层依赖 `wSkVaW_header` / `wSkVaW_tabs` 这两个 CSS Modules 类名，以及 `:has()` 支持（Chromium 105+ / Safari 15.4+）。宿主若改名，该层静默失效，但不会影响其他层。
- 去掉行内代码底色后，行内代码与其后的普通文字完全靠字形区分。若宿主将来取消文件提及的重写，这一层就只剩"把药丸去掉"这一个作用。

## 许可

MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

plugins.description: Hand a local file to any program's file picker: wait for the native Open dialog, paste the path through the clipboard, read it back to verify character by character, then confirm. The target is always explicit and every step leaves evidence.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-file-handover（递文件）

**把一个本地文件交给系统"打开文件"对话框** —— 网页上传、微信发文件、Photoshop 打开，
凡是"点一下、再在对话框里选文件"的地方，都由它代劳。

> 由来：AI 会点按钮、会打字，但**不会在文件选择器里选文件** —— 这是 GUI 自动化的最后一块空白。
> 我是在给自己做"发抖音"的时候撞上它的：投稿页的上传按钮点得响，弹出的系统对话框却进不去。

---

## 它做什么（五步，每步都回读）

| 步 | 动作 | 为什么要这样 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ① 等 | 轮询等 `#32770` 文件对话框出现（默认 30 秒） | 实测从点击到弹窗**可以超过 15 秒**，抢跑只会拿到空 |
| ② 认 | 在候选窗口里找**带文件名控件**（automation id `1148`）的那个 | 只认结构、不认标题 —— 跨语言，也绕开 `.ps1` 编码坑 |
| ③ 填 | **剪贴板粘贴**（全选 → 清空 → 粘贴）；另有 Win32 `SetWindowText` 与 UIA `ValuePattern` 两条备用路 | 打字不可信：这台机器的**中文输入法**会把打进去的 `\` `:` 变成全角标点和候选词（实测读回 `谢谢D：、但是、workspace、…`），剪贴板不过 IME |
| ④ 校 | **读回来逐字比对**，不一致就再来一轮（默认 3 轮） | 实测第 1、2 轮读回都是脏的，**第 3 轮才一致** —— 单次尝试真的不可信 |
| ⑤ 确认 | 按控件 id 找按钮（`1`=打开/保存、`2`=取消）并点击 | 盲发 Enter 不可靠，也挡不住输入法 |

**失败会带现场**：它把"看到过的每个候选窗口"和"每次尝试读回的实际值"一起返回，
所以排错不用猜。

## 安全边界

- **目标必须显式**：要交付的文件（`path`）必须是**绝对路径**；它**不会**自己去找"最像的对话框"。
- **默认不按标题过滤**：标题随语言/版本变化，是脆弱信号；要过滤就用 `expectTitle` 显式给。
- **不动手也能看**：`dryRun` 只探测（找对话框、报结构），不填不点。
- **只点它自己的对话框**：确认按钮只在①选中的那个对话框内部查找。

## 安装

市场收录后在 DSH 里搜 `dsh-file-handover` 安装。手动安装：

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-file-handover" -Target "D:\dsh\projects\dsh-file-handover"
# profile 的 package.json：dependencies 加 "dsh-file-handover": "link:D:/dsh/projects/dsh-file-handover"
# 并把 "dsh-file-handover" 加进 dsh.profile.bundles（漏了不加载）→ 重启 DSH
```

## 用法

### 工具

```
handover_file  path=<绝对路径>                        # 单个文件
handover_file  paths=[<绝对路径>, <绝对路径>, ...]      # 多选（v0.2.0，最多 12 个）
handover_file  path=... [timeoutSec] [dryRun] [expectTitle] [maxAttempts] [click]
```

**多选**（v0.2.0）：对话框支持多选时（网页的多图上传、微信发多个文件、系统"打开"框），
给 `paths` 数组即可。插件把路径按 `"a" "b" "c"` 的格式填进去，**逐个回读**——
少一个就算失败，不会出现"以为交了三个、实际只进了一个"。

典型配合（以网页上传为例）：

1. 用浏览器工具**真实点击**页面的"上传/选择文件"按钮（程序化 `input.click()` 不会弹出系统对话框）；
2. 调 `handover_file` 递文件（单个用 `path`，多个用 `paths`）；
3. 用浏览器工具**回读页面**，确认它真的收到了那些文件（名字/字节数）。

### 命令

```powershell
dsh-file-handover handover --path "D:\videos\a.mp4"
dsh-file-handover probe    --path "D:\videos\a.mp4"
dsh-file-handover handover --path "D:\a.mp4" --expect-title "Open" --no-click
```

退出码：`0` 已交付 / `1` 未完成 / `2` 用法错误。

## 它怎么实现的

宿主侧（Node）只做编排：校验参数、检查文件、起一个 **PowerShell** 子进程、解析它返回的 JSON。
真正碰 GUI 的是包内的 `lib/handover.ps1`（`UIAutomationClient` + `EnumWindows`）。

两个刻意的选择：

- **用 PowerShell 而不是原生模块**：Node 没有内置 Win32/UIA 绑定，而原生模块（ffi/winax）
  不能塞进一个纯 JS 插件。PowerShell 是 Windows 上唯一"零依赖"就能调 UIA 的通道。
- **脚本全 ASCII**：`.ps1` 若为无 BOM 的 UTF-8，Windows PowerShell 会按 GBK 读，
  脚本里的中文会变乱码、**所有按标题匹配的逻辑会静默失效**（实测：`打开` → `鎵撳紑`）。
  自测里有一条硬断言守着这个文件必须全 ASCII。

## 一次真实的实测记录（为什么上面那些边界长这样）

在一张真实的网页上传页上递一个 1MB 文件，这台机器上实际发生的事：

1. **第 1 轮**填完读回：
   `谢谢D：、但是、workspace、——test、upload-payload。斌谢谢D：D:\dsh\workspace\_test\upload-payload.bin`
   —— 中文输入法把打进去的字符变成了候选词和全角标点，而"全选"没生效，内容还在往后追加。
2. **第 2 轮**：`谢谢D：、但D:\dsh\workspace\_test\upload-payload.bin` —— 清空只生效了一半。
3. **第 3 轮**：✅ 逐字一致 → 才点确认 → 页面确认收到 `upload-payload.bin:1000000`。

所以这三件事不是设计洁癖，是被逼出来的：**③ 走剪贴板**（绕开输入法）、**④ 必须回读**（一次永远不算数）、
**⑤ 只认控件 id**（标题随语言变，认不起）。

## 0.1.2：两处"看起来成功"的修正（2026-10-17 真机事故）

1. **文件名框少走了一级**：现代文件对话框的结构是
   `dialog > ComboBoxEx32 > ComboBox > Edit`，而旧代码只找了 `ComboBoxEx32 > Edit`，
   于是 `FindFileEdit` 返回 0 —— **整条 win32 路径被静默跳过**，直接掉到"猜焦点"的剪贴板路径。
2. **回读不到就点确认**：剪贴板路径读不回文件名时，旧代码仍把这次填充算作"已填"并点了确认。
   真机后果：粘贴其实落在了**地址栏**（对话框跳到了目标文件夹），确认后对话框关了、**页面一个文件也没收到**，
   而工具回执写的是"成功"。现在：**回读不到 = 失败**，不点确认，把对话框留着让人看。

## 已知限制

- **仅 Windows**：依赖 `EnumWindows` / UI Automation / `powershell.exe`。
- **只认系统原生文件对话框**（窗口类 `#32770`）：应用自己画的（自绘）选择器不适用。
- **冷启动有开销**：每次调用会起一个 PowerShell 进程（数百毫秒到两秒）。
- **它不负责"触发"**：打开对话框的那一下（点按钮、快捷键、菜单）要由调用方先做 ——
  这样"目标显式"才守得住。

## 自测

```powershell
node test/smoke.mjs   # 不碰真实 GUI：PowerShell 用假 spawn 顶替；含干活脚本的静态检查
```

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Unified rail for the DSH sidebar: sort the top panels and the bottom actions as one list. / DSH 左侧栏统一排序插件：顶部面板与底部动作混排成同一条序列。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-railist

**English** | [中文](#中文)

---

## English

Manage the whole DSH left column as one list: reorder rows across the panel list and the footer action row, rename them, change their icons, hide them, and fold them into Groups. Everything is configured in a new Settings tab and applies immediately.

> A fork of [dsh-panellist](https://github.com/qwq1999/dsh-panellist). Upstream manages the panel list alone; this fork extends it to a single sequence spanning two seats.

---

## Features

- **One sequence across seats** — the panel list and the footer action row are sorted as a single list, so a row can be dragged from one into the other.
- **Reorder by drag** — drag any row to a new position; the rail follows the list live.
- **Rename and re-icon** — give any row your own label and pick its icon from a built-in set.
- **Show / hide** — take a row off the rail without uninstalling its plugin.
- **Groups** — fold several rows into one Group row with a flyout menu; ungroup at any time.
- **Appearance override** — adjust the rail's own look from the Settings tab.
- **Config file's full path** — shown in Settings so you can back it up or edit it.

The Settings row itself always stays last and cannot be dragged, and every change is written to disk only when you press Save.

## Screenshots

| Settings → Panel list | Appearance override | A Group menu on the rail |
| :-: | :-: | :-: |
| ![Settings → Panel list](docs/images/settings-panel-list.png) | ![Appearance override](docs/images/settings-appearance.png) | ![A Group menu on the rail](docs/images/rail-group-menu.png) |

## Installation

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-railist
```

Then restart DSH. To remove it:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-railist
```

## Compatibility

| Requirement | Version |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` |
| Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |
| Profile | `web` |
| Platform | Windows / macOS / Linux desktop |

## Configuration

Your settings live in `~/.dsh/railist.json`. The full path is also shown in the Settings tab. If a row's plugin is missing or disabled, the row is kept in the file and marked as missing rather than being deleted.

## License

MIT

---

## 中文

把 DSH 左侧栏当成一整条列表来管理：跨「面板区」与「底部动作区」调整顺序、重命名、换图标、隐藏，以及把若干行折叠成分组。全部在设置页完成，改完立即生效。

> 本项目 fork 自 [dsh-panellist](https://github.com/qwq1999/dsh-panellist)。上游只管理面板区；本 fork 把它扩展成跨越两个区域的同一条序列。

---

## 功能

- **跨区域同一条序列** —— 面板区与底部动作区当成一条列表排序，所以一个行可以从一个区域拖进另一个区域。
- **拖动排序** —— 把任意行拖到新位置，左侧栏实时跟随。
- **重命名与换图标** —— 给任意行起自己的名字，并从内置图标集里挑图标。
- **显示 / 隐藏** —— 把某一行从左侧栏隐藏，而不必卸载它的插件。
- **分组** —— 把若干行折叠成一个分组行（带展开菜单），随时可以解组。
- **外观覆盖** —— 在设置页调整左侧栏自身的外观。
- **配置文件全路径** —— 设置页直接显示，方便你备份或手动编辑。

「设置」那一行固定在最下方、不可拖动；所有改动都要点保存才会写进磁盘。

## 效果图

| 设置 → 面板列表 | 外观覆盖 | 左侧栏上的分组菜单 |
| :-: | :-: | :-: |
| ![设置 → 面板列表](docs/images/settings-panel-list.png) | ![外观覆盖](docs/images/settings-appearance.png) | ![左侧栏上的分组菜单](docs/images/rail-group-menu.png) |

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-railist
```

装完重启 DSH。卸载：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-railist
```

## 兼容版本

| 要求 | 版本 |
| --- | --- |
| DSH | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` |
| Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |
| Profile | `web` |
| 平台 | Windows / macOS / Linux 桌面端 |

## 配置

配置存在 `~/.dsh/railist.json`，设置页里也会显示完整路径。如果某一行的插件被卸载或停用，这一行会保留在配置里并标记为「已缺失」，不会被自动删掉。

## 许可证

MIT

plugins.description: 多机 dsh 控制：从本地一个窗口驱动你其他服务器上的 dsh——远端会话原生进侧栏，整台远端界面也能搬进来。· Control the dsh instances on your other machines from one local window.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-control

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**Every machine already runs dsh. Make this one window the front end for all of them.**

Chat with the dsh instances on your other machines, natively from your local sidebar.
Remote sessions stream back token by token; the remote uses its own model credentials,
tools and sandbox. Zero changes on the remote. Zero dependencies. One-line install.

![dsh-control in action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/hero.png)

*Two dsh windows answering the same question. The left window shows a session auto-named
`控制端·<local title>` (①) — that naming only happens on the machine the plugin drives. The right
window shows the workspace `cn-dsh2` the plugin created (②) and the model route set to the
environment name (③).*

> 🎬 A 15-second capture (one-click connect → streaming reply) is being recorded.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add github:6mt/dsh-control
```

Use the profile you already run (usually `web` or `desktop`). No build step, no native
modules, no dependencies — the plugin is plain JavaScript and installs as-is.

<details>
<summary>GitHub slow or blocked? Install from the release tarball instead</summary>

Download [dsh-control-0.2.0.tgz](https://github.com/6mt/dsh-control/releases/download/v0.2.0/dsh-control-0.2.0.tgz)
and run:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add ./dsh-control-0.2.0.tgz
```
</details>

After installing, **fully quit and reopen dsh** (⌘Q — closing the window is not enough),
then:

- Right sidebar →「远程 dsh 环境」→ type `user@host` → connect
- Left sidebar →「🌐 远程环境」→ pick the environment tab to enter the remote's full UI

> Upgrades need the same ⌘Q: a plugin's host half loads at process start.

> An npm package (`dsh-control`) is prepared and can be published later; the GitHub
> command above is the current install path.

## Install failed?

- **Retry once** — the install pulls the repo from GitHub and resolves peers from npm;
  on a bad network pnpm can time out.
- **Seeing `allowBuilds` / "prepare script"** — that is dsh's generic hint for *any*
  failed git-hosted install. This plugin has no build scripts (its only script is
  `test`), so nothing needs approving; just retry.
- Still stuck? Use the release tarball instead (above).

## Versions & updating

- **What you get**: `github:6mt/dsh-control` installs the newest commit of `main` and
  **pins it in your profile's lockfile** — it does not silently follow later commits.
- **Update**: `dsh plugin --profile <your profile> update dsh-control`
  *(pnpm re-resolves the git ref and pulls the new code)*
- **Pin a version**: `github:6mt/dsh-control#v0.2.0` (tag) or `github:6mt/dsh-control#<commit>`
- Changes are recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## How is this different from the same-named `dsh-control` skill?

There is another project called `jacjackai/dsh-control` — a **skill** that lets an AI agent
operate the DSH **on your own machine**. This repository is a **plugin** for a different
job: **across machines**. It brings the dsh instances you already run on other servers into
one local window (their sessions appear natively in the sidebar, and the whole remote UI
can be opened in place). The two can coexist.

## How is this different from dsh-remote / dsh-remote-ssh?

![How the two approaches differ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/compare.svg)

| | Remote-workspace plugins (dsh-remote, …) | **dsh-control** |
|---|---|---|
| The remote machine is a | **file system** (SFTP tool set) | **dsh that is already running there** |
| Sessions live | local session + remote directory | **remote sessions, native in your sidebar** |
| Credentials & tools | configured locally, SSH config duplicated | the remote's own — nothing copied |
| Remote needs | only SSH | dsh installed (≥0.2.0-rc.2) with its web instance running |
| Changes on the remote | some deploy dsh for you | **zero** (read-only probing + the remote's own API) |

The two **coexist** (tested side by side): no dsh on the remote → use dsh-remote;
dsh already there → use dsh-control.

## What it does

![The remote dsh environments panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/panel.png)

*The「远程 dsh 环境」panel: type `user@host` and connect — the row then reports its state and
whether the environment already has its workspace.*

- **One-click connect** — type `user@host`; the plugin probes the remote dsh, fetches
  its access token and opens an encrypted channel (~5 s)
- **Automatic workspace** — each environment gets a same-named local workspace; any
  session created inside it automatically becomes a remote session
- **True streaming** — remote replies flow in token by token, not dumped at the end
- **Paired naming** — remote sessions are named `控制端·<local title>`, so both sides match
- **Visible & self-healing** — remote sessions are marked in the sidebar; disconnects
  are reported honestly and repaired by one click

### The whole remote UI, brought inside

「🌐 远程环境」in the sidebar renders the remote machine's **complete dsh interface**
(workspaces, sessions, chat, settings) inside one local page, with a tab per environment:

![The remote environment page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/remote-env.png)

*A real run on the remote machine. ① the environment tab — one tab per machine;
② the remote's own workspaces and sessions; ③ a real session running there — subagents,
code blocks and model usage all inside the page; ④ open it in a standalone window.*

- **The real interface, not a re-implementation** — the remote dsh renders itself, so it
  tracks whatever version the remote runs
- **Same-origin proxy** — the page is served by your local web server; the remote's
  credentials are injected server-side, so the browser never sees a token and any auth
  shell in front of the remote is irrelevant (traffic reaches the remote's loopback
  through the encrypted channel)
- **Switching panels keeps it alive** — go handle a local session and come back; the
  remote view is still there, no reload, no reconnect
- **Compression kept for assets** — only the document is uncompressed (it gets
  instrumented); bundles keep gzip

## Security

**What it does on your machine**: one state file
(`$DSH_HOME/dsh-control/state.json`, mode 0600, holds the remote access tokens) and an
on-demand SSH tunnel process.
**What it never does**: no installs or writes on the remote, no lifecycle management of
the remote dsh, never reads your other local credentials, tokens never enter logs.
When passwordless SSH is not set up it shows the exact one-line fix — passwords are
never stored. Details in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Known limitations

- The remote must already run dsh (≥ 0.2.0-rc.2) with its web instance (otherwise use a
  remote-workspace plugin)
- Connects over SSH (passwordless or configured key; a no-SSH "direct address" mode is
  implemented but not yet exposed in the UI)
- The remote-environment page **is** the remote's own UI: actions there really affect the
  remote machine (exactly as if you opened it in a browser)
- The first visit loads the remote's front-end assets (a few seconds depending on the
  network); later visits do not reload
- Sidebar markers and the streaming feel are verified by eye per release
- Cancelling a remote turn is implemented but marked experimental

## Development

```sh
node --check lib/*.js
for t in test/*.test.mjs; do node "$t"; done   # 52 checks: unit / contract / structural invariants
scripts/verify-boot-selfheal.sh                # boot self-heal (needs a local dsh runtime)
```

## License

MIT © 6mt

plugins.description: Model-controlled context blocks for DeepSeek Harness PTC mode
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-block-ptc

**English | [中文](README.zh.md)**

[![CI](https://github.com/mengwEX/dsh-block-ptc/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mengwEX/dsh-block-ptc/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-block-ptc.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-block-ptc)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

Blackboard blocks for **PTC mode** in [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

Version `0.3.0` layers the block protocol on the built-in `run_code` transport.
DSH's PTC presentation allows only `run_code` to be called directly, so the
model declares blocks in the tool description:

```
run_code({ description: "[block: auth] Rework the auth tests", code })
```

A *block* is a blackboard region. Every program the model runs is tagged with
block ids, and when the block's work is finished the model hands in a summary
**it writes itself** — which then replaces that block's messages in the model's
own context. The original messages stay in the append-only session log, so the
human transcript keeps everything and replay stays deterministic.

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2 or newer**; no upper version bound
- Community plugin maintained by [mengwEX](https://github.com/mengwEX)
- **Zero runtime dependencies** — the only external import is `node:crypto`
- License: **MIT**

## Table of contents

- [Why](#why)
- [Context and cache comparison](#context-and-cache-comparison)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Install](#install)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Reference](#reference)
- [Design notes](#design-notes)
- [Verification](#verification)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
- [Known limits](#known-limits)
- [Development](#development)
- [License](#license)

## Why

Automatic compaction condenses history when token pressure builds, and it
decides what to condense by size. It has no idea that the last forty messages
were one finished sub-task and the next ten are a new one.

This plugin lets the model draw that line itself: open a block, work inside it,
and close it with a handover summary — so the context it keeps is the one it
chose to keep. The model submits the summary inside its program call; the plugin
does not run a separate summarizer model.

## Context and cache comparison

![Illustrative comparison of input context and modeled cache hits for the same synthetic conversation](docs/assets/context-comparison.en.png)

**Mechanism illustration, not an API benchmark.** Both panels replay the same
synthetic four-task workload with assigned token weights. Full bar = input
context; blue = modeled cache hits, orange = modeled cache misses. Cached tokens
still occupy the context window.

After a block closes, the next request carries a summary in place of its
completed work. Replacing history can also invalidate the cached suffix:
**smaller context does not guarantee a higher cache-hit rate or a lower bill**.
The closing assistant/tool pair settles before replacement; original user
messages remain. The baseline has not reached its automatic compaction threshold.

See the [data, assumptions and reproduction steps](docs/context-comparison/README.md).
The plugin's `tokensFreed` is not a provider cache-hit measurement.

## How it works

The model's whole surface is the built-in PTC transport plus one
program-callable:

```
run_code({ description: "[block: <ids>] <goal>", code })   the only tool it may call directly
await tools.block_summary({ ids, summary })                  callable from inside a program
```

1. The header in `run_code.description` names the blocks a program advances.
   Its ids apply to the complete assistant message, including preceding
   thinking/text, and its tool results. Calls in the same assistant message
   contribute the union of their ids.
2. `tools.block_summary({ ids, summary })` replaces the complete interval from
   the earliest to the latest occurrence of any target id with one summary.
3. The summary inherits the union of the interval's ids minus the target ids.
   It can participate in a later summary. A summary with no remaining ids stays.
4. If a tool pair in the interval is unfinished, the request is queued until
   its result lands. A protected system/developer message refuses the
   entire interval; no prefix is silently replaced.

```text
A A B A C B  -- summary([A]) --> S[B] C B
S[B] C B    -- summary([B]) --> T[C]
T[C]        -- summary([C]) --> U[]
A A B A C B -- summary([A, B]) --> S[C]
```

What the human sees afterwards: the transcript still shows every original
turn (the log is append-only); the model's next request shows the summary
instead. In the Web UI the summary renders as a compaction checkpoint node.

## Install

Requirements: DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.2` and its bundled runtime, with
Cordis `>=4.0.5`. Neither peer range has an upper version bound. The plugin
is a profile **bundle**: installing it adds one row to `dsh.profile.bundles`
and one new agent preset, `block-ptc`. It does not modify the shipped `ptc`
preset.

The version ranges allow newer hosts to load the plugin; they are not a record
of completed compatibility checks. Live host verification for this release used
DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`. DSH's plugin loader includes prereleases when evaluating its
peer ranges. The plugin checks the required tool/prompt methods before mounting
and the session methods before summarizing, and reports missing capabilities.
Method presence does not verify event semantics, preset configuration or model
behaviour; these still need validation when the host changes.

### From npm (recommended)

Find **dsh-block-ptc** in the Harness Plugin Manager and install it, or ask an
agent with the Plugin Manager tool enabled to install the bundle:

```
plugin_manager  install_bundle  dsh-block-ptc
```

The package is published on [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-block-ptc).
Restart the application after installation and select the **Block PTC** preset.

### From a local checkout

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mengwEX/dsh-block-ptc.git
```

Install the absolute checkout path through the Plugin Manager:

```
plugin_manager  install_bundle  /absolute/path/to/dsh-block-ptc
```

Both methods use pnpm in the target profile. The local form installs a `link:`
dependency for development. Versioned source archives are also available under
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/mengwEX/dsh-block-ptc/releases).

### Manual install (equivalent, if you prefer files)

In `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "dependencies": { "dsh-block-ptc": "link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-block-ptc" },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-block-ptc"] } }
}
```

then run pnpm in that directory.

### After installing

1. The preset appears in the session preset picker as **Block PTC**.
2. **Restart the application once.** The loader keeps a plugin module per
   resolved URL, and installing a bundle changes the composition; a running
   host keeps the old module generation until it restarts.
3. Start a session with the **Block PTC** preset.

### Uninstall

```
plugin_manager  remove_bundle  dsh-block-ptc
```

then restart. `plugin_manager set_bundle dsh-block-ptc enabled=false` disables
it without removing the package.

## Quick start

Say what you want done, then let it close the block when it finishes:

> Read the parser module, explain how the tokenizer works, then close the block
> and continue with the lexer.

You should see:

- the model calling `run_code` with a description such as
  `[block: tokenizer] Explain the tokenizer` for everything it runs;
- a closing call to `block_summary` whose return value is
  `{"replaced": 3, "tokensFreed": 346}` — how many messages were replaced and
  the estimated token count of the replaced messages (before counting the new summary);
- a `<block-summary>…</block-summary>` node sitting where those messages were.

If a program call is refused with *"every `run_code` description must start
with `[block: <ids>] <goal>`"*, that is the preset's guard working. Retry the
program with the header; the refused call itself is not t

plugins.description: Tree-shaped knowledge bases for DeepSeek Harness: a right-side canvas you edit by hand, plus tools the model reads and writes. Nodes carry a trigger line saying when they apply; a base can be injected in full or as an index.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-knowledge-canvas

## Notebook and attachment reading (0.4.0)

Diary bases open in a notebook view with a monthly catalog, readable pages, earlier/newer navigation, revision history, and send/drag to chat. Narrow panels provide a catalog button. Switch back to the knowledge canvas to edit. This is a presentation change: encryption, session isolation, node storage and model-call behavior remain unchanged.

DSH settings offer a per-workspace attachment policy: on-demand (default) or required. On-demand reading lets the model choose attachments; required reading includes supported text and images with explicit limits and increases token usage.

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

A knowledge base for DeepSeek Harness that the model retrieves from **by judgement, not by similarity** — and that you edit on a canvas in the sidebar.

## The problem

**You explain something, and the next conversation still does not know it — or worse, it thinks it does, and the note is stale.**

This is not a context-window problem. Measured in one workspace:

```
$ node report-kb-use.mjs
50 tool call(s) in the log, 1 session(s)
  写 13 次（ops / …）
  读 1 次（read-animation）
  ⚠ 先写后读：第一次写入之前没有读过
```

**13 writes, 1 read** — and that read was from a different base. Knowledge was *recorded* and never *used*. Recording is free: the model does it in passing. Using is the hard part: you have to know the entry exists, and which one still holds.

## What makes this different

Every node ends with a line beginning 「什么时候该想起它：」 — "when should this come to mind". That line is what the outline shows, so the model matches a situation rather than an embedding. When it picks wrong, you see the wrong node on the canvas and fix the sentence that misled it.

## On the panel

| Where | What |
| --- | --- |
| Top row | search, read counters, refresh |
| One row per base | title, read progress, one switch (does this conversation read it), `⋯` menu (rename, delete, colour, export) |
| Canvas toolbar | zoom, fit, **width** (the whole base's default width, not one node), shape, colour, layout |
| 「定位到…」 at the bottom | type an id to jump to that node |

| Gesture | Result |
| --- | --- |
| click a node | opens the editor; click again to close |
| Enter / Space (focused) | same, from the keyboard |
| Shift+Enter | start a link; Enter on the target finishes it |
| drag a node | moves it; the drop is written to `layout.json` |
| hold ~0.26 s then drag | draws a **link** (orange), not a re-parent |
| right-drag from a node | same link |
| **Alt + drag a node** | makes the target its parent (grey line) |
| right-click a node | menu: new child / change history |
| right-click empty canvas | menu: new top-level node |
| drag a node out to the input box | hands that node to the conversation |
| the three handles | width, height, both |

Node size means three things in order: this node → the base's default → the canvas zoom. The toolbar's 「宽度」 is the second one.

Four layouts: layers, radial, staircase, compact. Switching only recomputes the default placement.

## Install

```bash
npm install dsh-knowledge-canvas
```

Restart DSH once after installing; the 「知识库」 panel appears in the sidebar. Panel-side changes need only a page reload; host-side changes (`index.js`, `lib/*`) need a restart — that distinction decides what you do after editing.

The first time you open a workspace, a base called 「怎么用这个知识库」 is seeded with everything the panel can do. It upgrades with each release, and nodes you edited are never overwritten.

## Tools the model gets (eight)

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `knowledge_read` | read a base or a node; without `base`, list the bases |
| `knowledge_create_base` | create a base with a root node. **Usable immediately** — no `knowledge_select` needed |
| `knowledge_write_node` | write or edit a node. The return carries the id it just created, ready to use as `parent` |
| `knowledge_link` | connect two nodes, and say in one line why they are related |
| `knowledge_remove_node` | mark a node removed (recoverable, not deleted) |
| `knowledge_unlink` | remove an association; the nodes stay, the dashed line goes |
| `knowledge_select` | switch a base on or off for this conversation |
| `knowledge_remove_base` | mark a base removed (recoverable; the file is not deleted) |
| `knowledge_show_images` | Hands a node's pictures to the model as images |

## Settings, per workspace

Settings → 知识库, one block per workspace: the workspace's path, a **记录调用过程** switch (off by default; when on, every tool call is logged and the panel shows 「正在检索 n3（…）」), and per-base index/full switches.

The workspace list is **the directories in the session list ∪ the directories on disk that have `.dsh-knowledge/`** — the second set is recovered from `$DSH_HOME/sessions/`, where each session has a directory named after its workspace path with separators turned into `-`.

## Diary mode (optional)

For people who do not want to organise notes — they want something to remember. A switch at the top of the panel, **per conversation**.

With it on, that conversation writes an entry of its own when a stretch of talk reaches a place worth keeping. Not daily. Not in other conversations.

- **One per conversation**: `diary-<hash>.json`. The switch is per conversation and so is the data — another conversation in the same workspace neither sees it nor can read it.
- **Stored sealed** (AES-256-GCM). A model that `cat`s the file gets base64.
- **The prompt gives conventions, not a voice.** The persona is yours; the plugin does not write letters on your behalf.

## What it will not do

- **It is not a chat log.** Nothing is captured automatically; only what you or the model explicitly write.
- **It does not sync anywhere.** Everything is under `<workspace>/.dsh-knowledge/`, plain JSON: open it in Notepad, commit it, copy the folder. No account, no server.
- **The diary's sealing stops accidents, not readers.** The key is derived from the base name, so anyone who reads this source can decrypt. Stopping a model that goes looking needs a key that never touches the disk — a password or an OS credential — which is a different design.
- **It does not write a persona.** Diary mode injects writing conventions, not a tone.
- **No full-text search.** The box does substring matching over titles and bodies; no index, no embeddings.

## Where the files are

```
<workspace>/.dsh-knowledge/
├── <base id>.json        one file per base: nodes, links, seed fingerprint
├── selection.json        which bases this workspace reads, how they are injected, call logging
├── layout.json           positions, widths, shapes, colours
├── .sessions/<id>.json   this conversation's own switches (including the diary)
└── activity.log          tool-call records, only while call logging is on
```

- **Host** (`index.js`, `lib/*`): injection, tools, routes, the seeded tutorial, the diary conventions.
- **Panel** (`client.js`): canvas, gestures, editor, settings. **It reads those JSON files directly**, not through the host — so when the panel "cannot see a base", check what it read, not what the host answered.
- The outline is assembled before every model call and holds titles, summaries and trigger lines; bodies need an explicit `knowledge_read`.

### For contributors

- `npm run check:all` runs four things: identifiers, sprite aspect ratios, a public-tree check (no local paths, addresses or private ids), and its assertions over store/routes/tools (the count is what the run prints).
- **Change a gesture, change the tutorial line that describes it** (`lib/seed.js`, the table at the top), or the tutorial describes something that does not exist.
- The tutorial is recognised **by content** (whichever base shares most of the seed's node ids), not by file name — that rule came from three workspaces keeping it under three different names.

## Development

```bash
npm run check:all     # identifiers + sprites + public tree + assertions
npm test              # assertions only
```

Publishing needs a real terminal (2FA needs a TTY), and after publishing the version stays `Validating` until npm's automated review finishes:

```bash
cd <this repo>
npm publish

plugins.description: Runtime evidence that helps agents trace, profile, and burn down hotspots in application and native code, GPU kernels, and inference stacks.
plugins.readme_text:
flameox

Bounded local runtime evidence for coding agents.

Flameox coordinates profilers, benchmark tools, trace processors, and direct local targets. It turns an explicit artifact or command into bounded evidence while keeping durable preservation optional. The agent chooses hypotheses and experiments; Flameox records observed inputs, execution provenance, typed evidence, coverage, and limitations. There is no workspace to initialize or project configuration to maintain. Pass exact artifact paths to analysis and an explicit argv plus absolute working directory to capture. Flameox does not search parent directories, edit project files, or provide a hosted service. ## Quick start Configure an MCP client with the global setup command: ```console npx flameox@latest setup ``` Setup detects supported clients and asks which configurations to update. For automation, select clients explicitly, for example `--client codex --yes` or `--all --yes`; `--dry-run` reports the paths and actions without writing. Setup preserves unrelated client configuration and does not change project files. See [the npm package guide](npm/README.md) for details. Update existing MCP registrations with: ```console npx flameox@latest update ``` `update --check` reports available updates without changing configuration. Updates preserve each client's provider extras and settings, verify the new environment before changing release pins, and report which clients need a restart or reconnect. Use `--client codex` to select one client, or `--version 0.2.8` to select a specific release, including for rollback. The Python CLI exposes the same `flameox update` command. For direct CLI use, pass exact artifact paths or an explicit command: ```console uvx flameox analyze preview_artifact /absolute/path/to/artifact.json uvx flameox capture --provider direct --cwd "$PWD" -- python benchmark.py ``` To launch the stdio MCP server manually: ```console uvx flameox mcp serve ``` For local development, clone the repository, install its development dependencies, and inspect the available tools: ```console git clone https://github.com/morluto/flameox.git cd flameox uv sync --extra dev --extra memory --extra trace --extra cpu uv run flameox mcp inspect ``` ## Evidence and storage Analysis and unpreserved capture use bounded session scratch. Session `analysis_id` values expire when evicted or when the server stops. Explicit preservation creates the user-level Flameox data directory and stores native bytes and a canonical evidence bundle by SHA-256. Set `FLAMEOX_DATA_DIR` to choose another location. Preservation is optional; it does not imply full console-output retention. Flameox distinguishes observed, derived, and inferred claims. Profiles guide exploration but do not establish causality or performance improvement. Confirmatory claims require representative workloads, declared metrics and estimands, compatible identities, preserved samples, and a semantic oracle. ## MCP The MCP server has no workspace binding. It exposes named analysis and capture tools through the same operation registry as the CLI. Analysis tools accept explicit sources; capture tools accept a typed target and provider. Tool schemas expose operation-specific fields directly. Inspect the catalog with `flameox mcp inspect`; use `--tool TOOL_NAME` for focused schemas and examples. The complete contract and current tool catalog are in [the interface guide](docs/interfaces.md). Tools return their full bounded results inline, including failures and recovery actions. Preserved evidence has a durable `evidence_id`; `inspect_evidence` returns its redacted metadata and replay sources inline. Capture takes argv, not a shell string. A direct target supplies an absolute working directory and bounded environment overrides. Results may include `next_page`; replay its named analysis tool and arguments unchanged. Capture continuations read collected artifacts and do not rerun the target. MCP work belongs to the live request, so cancellation applies directly and no detached job survives a restart. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) describes process and package boundaries. - [Storage and evidence](docs/storage-and-evidence.md) defines preservation and provenance. - [Investigations](docs/investigations.md) covers experiments, comparison, and evidence quality. - [Adapters](docs/adapters.md) documents provider compatibility and integration policy. - [Runtime safety](docs/runtime-safety.md) covers limits, recovery, integrity, and privacy. - [Interfaces](docs/interfaces.md) defines CLI and MCP contracts. - [Testing](docs/testing.md) describes test selections and known proof gaps. ## Development Flameox requires Python 3.12 or newer and uses the committed `uv.lock`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and contribution guidance. ```console uv run ruff check src tests tools uv run ruff format --check src tests tools uv run mypy src tests tools uv run pytest -q ``` Flameox is licensed under the MIT License.

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.
